title: Exact commit
text: An item QA case selects one registered lane under the caller's matching item/task claim. Branch, checkout path and commit come from that same row, including a missing commit. Multiple lanes require an unambiguous selection; CI refuses explicit checkout, branch or SHA disagreement before publication. CI publishes an immutable commit, then stamps it through the existing snapshot authority only when the selected live checkout has the matching branch and clean exact HEAD. Missing or mismatched checkouts never supply a stamp. A stale durable head can be repaired with snapshot sync --head-only after verifying the already-published passing candidate, without rerunning its gate. The configured release-time exact-pair gate owns default consumer proof; item merges need no separate consumer build. Explicitly requested consumer product_ref inputs name an exact pushed producer commit or main, resolved on each execution to the producer repository main SHA before dispatch: QA verifies it on the producer remote before dispatch. An existing product_repo workflow input identifies that repository; otherwise one upstream cross-project companion project supplies its binding. Missing or ambiguous identity and unreadable or unpublished commits refuse with recovery. The consumer receives the gate-pushed commit after any producer rebase. The run writer observes the start commit when available and never replaces a verified commit. The latest pass on an effective item requirement remains accepted at merge and done without comparing commits; required queue CI still tests the final commit. Explicitly cancelled runs keep their cancelled conclusion even when no job started and are never retried as runner starvation. Recording a newer commit wait retires the session's unnotified waits of the same repository and gate kind for other known commits. A cancelled-run notice directs the worker to the current lane head and its evidence instead of re-dispatching the cancelled commit. A replayed workflow-dispatch request returns its existing run while that run is active or has a verdict (success or failure); only a run that ended with no verdict (cancelled, startup failure, timeout) advances to a new attempt, and only for the request's owner. One rule picks the run that proves a commit for merge verification, release creation and the deploy-time CI gate: the newest run and attempt of the ci_workflow_file workflow on exactly that commit whose event is not pull_request, pull_request_target or merge_group, from whichever branch started it. Merge verification's dispatch on the lane branch therefore proves the identical merged commit at delivery with no second dispatch, and a newer failed, cancelled or unfinished attempt is never passed over for an older green one. Proof never establishes release ancestry or member containment.
